I firmly believe that the ideal way to arrive at the best conclusions (especially in politics) is by forging one's views on the anvil of vigorous debate (hence the title). In furtherance of that and to foster some discussion around here not based around individual news articles, I'll periodically start such discussions with these posts, probably about once a week from now on, since I've seen some more interest in non-link posts.

This week: civilian armaments, also framed as "gun control" or "gun rights." Some questions to consider:

  • Should there be any limits on use (e.g. concealed carry, open carry)?

One thing that rarely gets brought up is that for all of the advances in electric car technology, ICE engine technology has been innovating at a similarly rapid rate. The new 2016 Ford Fiesta has an engine that is vastly more efficient, cheap, and high quality than those of 20 years ago. The same is true for solar and wind energy, where the petroleum industry regularly sinks billions into R&D. Of course, these forces are what propels technology forward.
